title: Stream sink contracts and SDK ergonomics (scratchpad)
body:
Status: rough product sketch / engineering-friendly notes
Owner: Aisha Patel (product)
Purpose: capture a compact, pragmatic protocol for "stream sinks" — small immutable output frames that represent either partial prose, structured records, or tool-call intents — and describe SDK ergonomics and migration guidance for client authors. This is intentionally lightweight: goal is a minimal-surface compatibility layer that supports low-bandwidth clients, resumable sessions, tool handoffs, and structured validation without heavy frame formats.

Background and motivation
- Problem space: Many host API customers are building interactive experiences that need partial, deterministic results and to orchestrate tool calls from model output. Current streaming proposals are rich but heavyweight for mobile/edge clients and make resume/replay complex. We want a compact contract that:
  - expresses incremental content and typed tool calls
  - supports cheap checkpoint/resume and idempotent replay
  - keeps SDK ergonomics predictable (easy to consume in JS/Swift/Go)

High-level idea
- Stream sink: an append-only sequence of small frames emitted by the model server. Each frame is one of: TEXT_CHUNK, STRUCT_RECORD, TOOL_INTENT, METADATA (progress/hints), or FINAL_COMMIT. Frames are self-describing, small (<= 4KB typical), and include a monotonically increasing frame_id and optional parent reference for branching.
- Clients attach a small session token and an optional resume_cursor (last seen frame_id). Server will send later frames starting after resume_cursor. If resume_cursor missing server starts from frame 0.
- Tool intents are separate, structured frames that carry a typed contract (name, inputs json-schema, suggested confidence) and an intent_id. Clients can accept, decline, or request clarification. Acceptance emits an acceptance-frame back to the server, which acts as a durable event (useful for audits / replay).

Goals (measurable)
- Latency: first TEXT_CHUNK within 150ms for typical short responses (8–32 tokens).
- Resume correctness: client resume works without duplication or loss in >99.9% of session reconnections in 24h run.
- Developer ergonomics: we provide a single SDK-level callback model (onFrame) and short helpers for common patterns (onTextDelta, onRecord, onToolSuggestion).
- Backwards compatibility: allow existing streaming users to adopt incrementally via a compatibility switch (frame envelope v1).

Non-goals
- Full conversational state sync (we will not attempt CRDT-style merging).
- Rich transactional semantics spanning multiple tool calls; the system offers durability and idempotency guidance but not a full distributed transaction manager.

Frame format (compact JSON envelope) - example (human readable):
{
  "frame_id": "0000000124",
  "type": "TEXT_CHUNK",
  "session_id": "s-83j3",
  "payload": "...delta text...",
  "parent_frame_id": "0000000123",
  "timestamp": "2025-03-03T15:21:08Z",
  "signature": "optional-sig"
}
Notes: payloads for STRUCT_RECORD and TOOL_INTENT contain a small JSON body with schema version metadata. We deliberately keep no binary blobs; attachments handled by out-of-band signed urls.

Tool intent contract
- TOOL_INTENT frame fields: intent_id, tool_name (string), schema_version, inputs (json), suggested_confidence (float 0–1), explanation_text (optional).
- Client responses: ACCEPT_INTENT (intent_id, actor, timestamp), DECLINE_INTENT (intent_id, reason), REQUEST_CLARIFY (intent_id, clarifying_prompt). These are sent on the control channel (HTTP POST) and also emit small ACK frames into the stream so other subscribers see state changes.
- Idempotency: intent_id must be a stable UUID emitted by server; client acceptance includes an idempotency token for retries.

Structured output and schema negotiation
- Each STRUCT_RECORD frame includes a record_type and schema_uri (semver). Client SDKs will expose a small validator that checks incoming records and can map unknown fields into a raw bag.
- Version negotiation is optimistic: client can request a 'schema_policy' in session creation (strict|lenient) — default lenient. Strict clients receive validation failures as METADATA frames flagged with error_level=ERROR.

SDK ergonomics (JS/Swift/Go recommended patterns)
- Minimal API (pseudocode):
  const s = client.stream({sessionId, resumeCursor, schemaPolicy: 'lenient'})
  s.onFrame(frame => { switch(frame.type) { case 'TEXT_CHUNK': handleDelta(frame.payload); break; case 'STRUCT_RECORD': upsertRecord(frame.payload); break; case 'TOOL_INTENT': showToolCard(frame.payload); break; }});
  s.acceptIntent(intentId).then(...)
- Backpressure: SDK exposes a pluggable backpressure policy. Default: buffer up to N frames (N=64) and apply coalescing for TEXT_CHUNK deltas (merge subsequent small deltas if client CPU high).
- Checkpointing helpers: SDK provides saveCursor() -> lastSeenFrameId and resumeFrom(cursor). We will surface one-line code examples for mobile and server.
- Offline-first hint: when network unreliable, SDK will switch to a small local cache of last 128 frames and show a local replayable transcript; on reconnect, SDK will automatically resume and reconcile any acceptance ACKs.

Observability and ops
- Telemetry events to emit: frame_emitted (type, size, latency_ms), session_resume_attempt (success|fail), intent_accepted (intent_id), schema_validation_error (record_type).
- Sampling: frame_emitted sampled at 0.1 for TEXT_CHUNK, 1.0 for TOOL_INTENT/STRUCT_RECORD.
- Dashboards: new per-session timeline view in Console showing frame types and last 10 ACKs. Useful for debugging partial outputs and tool flakiness.

Migration / rollout plan
- Phase 0: internal dogfood + SDK alpha (2 weeks) — integrate with sandboxed conversations and a small mobile demo app.
- Phase 1: beta opt-in for customer apps (4 weeks) — compatibility mode enabled at call-level. Collect production metrics.
- Phase 2: default streaming protocol for new sessions (8 weeks) — old streaming kept behind a legacy flag for 3 months.

Security and audit considerations
- Tool intents are sensitive: default retention short (30 days) unless customer requests longer. Intent acceptance events are auditable and include actor metadata.
- Signed integrity token optional on frames for high-assurance deployments (private / dedicated).

Open questions / tradeoffs (need triage)
- How large should default frame size be? 4KB is a guess. Need perf tests across mobile and 1Gbs/5G networks.
- Should acceptance ACKs travel on the same stream or via separate control plane? Pros/cons: same-stream keeps single timeline; separate control plane reduces ordering coupling.
- Schema lifecycle: do we support server-initiated schema migrations where old records are auto-mapped? Harder but nicer UX.
- Ownership of tool invocation side effects: should server attempt to execute accepted tool intents (service-level) or simply produce events for customer-run tool runners? Mixed mode?

Next steps / action items
- Engineering: perf microbench for small frames and resume scenarios (Connor) — JIRA-PROD-4123 assigned.
- SDK: implement minimal JS streaming client with saveCursor/resume + tiny helper for tool-accept flow (Lina).
- Product: finalize acceptance UX pattern for tool cards and default timeouts for intent acceptance (Aisha).
- SRE/Privacy: propose retention and signed-frame modes for Private/Dedicated customers (Marco).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally a small-surface protocol focused on practical trade-offs. Looking for feedback on: accept/reject for frame types, preferred default sizing and resume semantics, and whether ACKs should be separate control-plane calls.
- Slack thread: #prod-hosted-api (search "stream sink api")

Rough timeline suggestion: 10-week iteration from alpha to soft-beta if we lock frame envelope v1 in 2 weeks.

-- end scratchpad --
